question: Where does the root of the bus rod sit inside 68's coaxial bracket over the drag CYCLE once the liner's contact with the Ti channel at the exit is an elastic-layer contact — and what are its patch, its edge pressure, its in-contact sliding and the terms that move the root besides the contact's give (00_07 HW.34 / HW.23)

inputs.source: geometry, member EI, pogo force, µ and µ_c sweeps, constraint factors imported from 55_bus_mechanical.py; the coaxial bracket, the plays and the pad-couple rows loaded from 68's cache; 55's wear rows loaded from its cache
inputs.geometry: shipped — the whole lock shank (HW.26 G1)

wear_path.reading: the cycle peak (touchdown) on a rigid wall receded by w at the exit; the slope assumes the receded wall follows the rod's touchdown shape back to the mouth (a conformal flare) — a short scar moves the touchdown to its rim and climbs less, so it is an UPPER bound; past the mouth's engagement the touchdown is at the mouth and the peak stops rising, and 68's upper end needs the MOUTH to wear as well

wear_readings.reading: frictionless kinematic sliding (a ceiling), on an unworn wall; the landing at each reversal of the drag (impact / partial-slip fretting) is not modelled

summary: Coaxial pogo drag, unworn wall, flush exit with a rounding. (A) The liner gives 0.27–0.40 µm at full drag against a 150 µm wall. (B) The cycle PEAK sits at or just after touchdown: 3.409–3.471 MPa, ×1.003–1.021 of 68's 3.4 MPa — on a rigid wall at the same edge it is F_td·L, the edge radius lifting it by ≤ 0.074 MPa over the flush value, and while the patch is tiny the give lifts it by ≤ 0.008 MPa more (68's sign). (C) On the LOADED part the sign turns: at full drag the compliance lowers the root by 0.11–0.21 MPa against a rigid wall at the same edge — the opposite sign to 68's 3EI·(R/k)/L², because the patch spreads inside the bore — and deepens the sub-cycle (touchdown → full drag) up to ×2.8 of the rigid one. (D) The bracket's upper end is not an elastic state: the peak climbs ≤ 0.136 MPa per µm of exit wear (a conformal-flare bound), the mouth engages after 50 µm and the peak saturates at 10.24 MPa; 68's 23.78 MPa needs 33 µm of MOUTH wear on top. (E) Edge peak at µ 0.5, 0.001 mm step, worst row: r 0.05 mm → 90 MPa · r 0.1 mm → 74 MPa · r 0.2 mm → 60 MPa · r 0.3 mm → 54 MPa · r 0.5 mm → 47 MPa; below 1·σ_y (23 °C tensile) at every swept radius; the elastic patch is ×26–39 55's flow bound. (F) The frictionless sliding — a kinematic ceiling — is at most 1/14 of 55's upper end, and the compliance carries 15%–68% of it against a rigid wall at the same edge (more at a tighter edge). (G) A pogo contact off the rod axis by ±0.5 mm moves the MEAN of a reversing cycle by -2.46 MPa and leaves its amplitude at 3.43 MPa (on axis 3.43); the exit section then carries ≈ the couple, 5.1 MPa nominal. (H) Lumped full-stick friction (an upper estimate) widens the loading/unloading loop to ≤ 1.37 MPa and moves the peak to full drag at r 0.05, 0.1 mm. (I) The ratified countersink is CONDITIONAL: the tip is past the bore line already at touchdown (0.8–2.6 µm), so a ring whose bore equals the channel's is the FIRST contact, which no model here has; only for a ring that clears it do the rows hold — peak ×1.030–1.102 of 68's figure, the full-drag moment reversing beyond e ≈ 1.29 mm, the sub-cycle up to 5.39 MPa, the sliding up to 1/4 of 55's upper end. (J) A sharp Ti edge INSIDE the layer (the countersink's, the mouth's) is a punch edge — peak ×1.41 per halving of the step; the flush sharp corner of the shipped CAD is outside the kernel, bounded only for a frictionless contact. MODELLED, not measured; no radius is proposed — the trade it names is weighed by a measured wear rate and slip regime, not by this model.

not_modelled.plasticity: linear elastic; a peak above the flow pressure is flagged, never redistributed
not_modelled.layer_shape: flat, uniform layer: the tube's curvature (a cylindrical confined column is ≈ 1.14× more compliant — δ_c may be ~14 % low) and its free end at the pad plane are not modelled; rows with r < t sit nearest that end and their peak is biased high
not_modelled.flush_sharp_corner: outside the kernel (it continues the layer past the pad plane); for coplanar free faces on a FRICTIONLESS counterface the corner stress is bounded (the reflected wedge is 180° with both faces free); under stick the corner is a clamped–free 90° wedge, weakly singular (≈ ρ^−0.35 at ν 0.4)
not_modelled.base: the hot-mounted tube grips the wire by interference — neither bonded nor frictionless; both are reported as a bracket
not_modelled.creep: the 20-yr relaxed modulus (lib PEEK_RELAX_FLOOR, a constant-strain figure) is used for a constant-load contact by linear-viscoelastic correspondence; it LOWERS the edge peak, so for the peak it is the anti-conservative end
not_modelled.friction: not in the solve; a lumped couple at the patch centroid, rigid in shear, from zero to full stick capped at µ_c·R·r_OD (µ_c from 55's PEEK–Ti sweep) — an upper estimate; the sliding figures are frictionless kinematic ceilings
not_modelled.thermal_axial_pdelta: no thermal term (the cold liner's ≈ 1 µm radial pull-back per 40 K moves 68's lower end by ≈ 0.13 MPa), no P-δ of the 1 N axial pogo force
not_modelled.wear: no wear in the contact solve; block wear_path is a rigid wall receded at the exit as a conformal flare (an upper bound of the slope — a short scar climbs less), and past the mouth's engagement it reports the saturation, not a two-station solve
not_modelled.ring_and_closure: the countersink's PEEK ring and the ratified exit closure element are not modelled; the tip is past the bore line already at touchdown, so a ring whose bore equals the channel's is the FIRST contact and every countersink row holds only for a ring that clears it
not_modelled.pad_couple: the reversing cycle's extremes are taken at touchdown on each wall (closed form, elastic = rigid there); the path between, with the − wall in play, is not solved
not_modelled.mouth: the mouth (the station under a channel offset) is not computed here
not_modelled.landing: each reversal of the drag lands the tube on the opposite wall; the impact / partial-slip fretting of that landing is not modelled
